thread:
mira: Heads-up — running into stale API key after hot-reloading the FastAPI dev server. I change REDWOOD_API_KEY in the shell, uvicorn reloads, but async Client still sends the old key.

jon: Is the client created at import time? paste minimal repro if possible.

mira: Yep, here's the repro we pared down to: 

mira: ```python
# app.py (client at import time)
from redwood import Client
client = Client()  # picks up REDWOOD_API_KEY from env

async def ping():
    await client.generate("hello")
```

mira: Steps: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyA -> uvicorn --reload app:app -> call /ping (returns ok) -> export REDWOOD_API_KEY=keyB -> uvicorn triggers reload -> call /ping -> still uses keyA.

sam: This is consistent with worker/reload lifecycles. Long-lived client objects can cache credentials and connection pools; when a new process is forked or modules are reimported, the old cached auth or sockets may persist.

jon: Passing api_key explicitly to Client() avoids env lookup. But I know it's annoying to change dozens of import-time constructors.

mira: Exactly. We have many modules and tests that rely on env-based instantiation.

sam: Quick workaround: lazy get_client that compares os.environ each call and recreates client if key changed. Example: 

sam: ```python
from redwood import Client
import os
_client = None

def get_client():
    global _client
    key = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY")
    if _client is None or getattr(_client, "_api_key", None) != key:
        _client = Client(api_key=key)
    return _client
```

jon: For the SDK fix, two options: (A) default provider reads env on every request when api_key not passed (more surprising but convenient), or (B) expose an async refresh() to rebind credentials and recreate pools for long-lived clients. Thoughts?

mira: I prefer (B) — explicit refresh is safer and less surprising.

sam: Agreed. Also need to document the caveat for import-time singletons and uvicorn/gunicorn forks. Refresh should rebuild connection pools/sessions to avoid reusing sockets with stale headers.

jon: I'll draft a PR that: 1) adds Client.refresh_credentials() async method, 2) ensures refresh reinitializes HTTP connector/pool and header cache, 3) includes tests reproducing uvicorn --reload and gunicorn worker fork scenarios. I'll reference the related GH issue.

devex-bot: Related issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412 (auth: long-lived client env rotation). Please link when opening PR. :link: 

mira: One more gotcha: in our dev setup we run gunicorn with uvicorn workers; those fork semantics can preserve file descriptors — rebuilding the pool is necessary, otherwise even a new client may handshake over an inherited socket with old auth state.

ops-bot: Heads-up: changing default auth semantics could affect enterprise customers relying on automatic rotation. Recommend feature-flagged rollout and config flag for Dedicated/Private so infra teams can opt in.

jon: Good point. PR will default to no behavioral change; refresh() will be opt-in. We can add an env var REDWOOD_CLIENT_AUTO_REFRESH (off by default) for experimental rollout.

mira: I'll open an issue with our internal logs and help validate the test matrix once the PR is up. happy to help test. :+1:

jon: assigning @sam to shepherd the PR and @mira to validate with the uvicorn/gunicorn repro.
